transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just feel like... like I got a motor running inside me all day. If I have to sit still for anything—like at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just sitting at home—I start feeling trapped. I just have to get up and do something. I can't just stay put.
How long have you been experiencing this restless feeling?

It's been this hard to manage for... I'd say about two years and two months. That's right around the time my older relative's health changed. I had to step up and take on a lot more responsibilities for them, and ever since then, that restless feeling has just been really bad.
Growing up, before the age of 12, did you have trouble with restlessness or difficulty sitting still?

Yeah, I did. Back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always moving my seat around. I just... I couldn't stay put. I'd talk out of turn, and I was always getting in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. So, yeah, it's been like that since I was a kid.
Do you also find it difficult to focus, organize your tasks, or follow through on details?

No, I wouldn't really say I have trouble with that. I mean, I can keep track of what needs getting done, especially with taking care of my relative. I don't really lose focus or get mixed up with the details of things. It's really just... it's just the needing to move all the time. My mind stays on track fine, it's just my body that won't stay put.
